references.text: Here it refers to how Jesus instituted the Lord's Supper during the Passover meal, which points back to the Passover celebration in Egypt.
This verse concerns David's prophecy about Judas' betrayal, which is closely linked to the event where Jesus breaks the bread.
Isaiah's prophecy about the Messiah being wounded for our transgressions and crushed for our sins, which corresponds with Jesus' words that the bread is his body, given for many.
Matthew gives a parallel account of the institution of the Lord's Supper, emphasizing its significance.
Luke's account of the Lord's Supper also includes Jesus' words about the bread as his body, referring to the same event.
Mark's version of the Lord's Supper, which also highlights Jesus' words that the bread symbolizes his body.
Paul refers to the Lord's Supper in 1 Corinthians, confirming the tradition and significance of this act.
